chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about the woman in postnatal bleeding: how long does she refrain? He said: Indeed, Asma' bint 'Umays was instructed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to perform ghusl after eighteen days, and there is no harm in her taking an extra precaution by one day or two days.

So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports that we have presented, because we have several approaches in discussing these reports. One of them is that these reports are solitary reports, differing in wording and contradictory in meaning; it is not possible to act upon all of them because of their contradiction, nor upon some of them, because some of them are no more deserving of being acted upon than others. The earlier reports are agreed upon regarding what they contain, because there is no disagreement that the days of menstruation are taken into consideration in postnatal bleeding; disagreement exists only concerning what exceeds that. When they conflict, it becomes necessary to leave acting upon them and to act upon what is agreed upon, as has been explained elsewhere. The second approach is that we carry these reports upon a kind of taqiyyah, because they agree with the position of the generality, and for that reason they differ just as the generality differ regarding the maximum days of postnatal bleeding, as though each of them gave a ruling according to the school he held. The third is that the reports were issued due to a particular circumstance, namely that they were asked about a woman upon whom these days had passed and in which she had not prayed, so they said at that point that she should perform ghusl and pray. And they did not say in any of them that this was a fixed limit such that considering less than it would not be permissible. That which indicates this meaning is what...

key_terms.آحَادٍ: solitary reports not reaching broad concurrence
key_terms.أَيَّامِ ٱلْحَيْضِ: the menstrual days used as a benchmark in this legal discussion
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلَ: to perform ghusl after the relevant period
key_terms.مُجْمَعٌ عَلَى مُتَضَمَّنِهَا: agreed upon in what they indicate
key_terms.ٱلتَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in expression of a ruling
key_terms.ٱلْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted hadith reports under discussion

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the maximum number of days of nifas and reconcile conflicting reports?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling on the maximum duration of nifas and cites a narration concerning Asma' bint 'Umays. It then explains methods for reconciling conflicting reports by preferring what is agreed upon, considering taqiyyah, or understanding some narrations as answers tied to a particular circumstance rather than fixed limits.
